- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2% downward bias for mid-term horizon (14–30 days).
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment environments; increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment <0.4 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., 0.6→0.8 in 3 days), model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent price momentum; if last 3–5 days show strong trend, apply a 1–2% mean-reversion correction if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
